reason: The cited evidence does not directly support the key mechanistic premises. E1 only describes pure tungsten's DBTT problem, E2 lists unrelated HEA compositions and properties, and E3 reports creep data for different alloys (HfTaTiVZr, TaTiVWZr) at lower temperatures (up to 573 K) without addressing lattice distortion effects on toughness or ductility. None of the passages provide evidence for the claimed heterogeneous energy landscape, distributed dislocation activation, or comparative toughness enhancement in WTaTiVZr.
premises: Severe lattice distortion in equimolar WTaTiVZr creates a heterogeneous energy landscape for dislocations
This heterogeneity impedes abrupt dislocation motion and promotes strain hardening
Distributed dislocation activation delays crack nucleation and propagation at high temperature
Pure tungsten has a relatively homogeneous and brittle dislocation response
The proposed mechanism will yield higher plastic strain and toughness in the HEA vs. pure W at 800–1000°C
